title: El expreso
goal: Buy a ticket to Managua and pick the right bus
culture: The expreso does not stop; the ordinario stops for anybody who waves and takes twice as long to save you about a dollar. The timetable on the wall is from another year, so ask the woman and not the wall.

beats.good: Un boleto — one ticket. In a bus terminal it is very nearly the only sentence you strictly need.
El expreso does not stop. El ordinario stops for everybody who waves at it and takes twice as long to save you about a dollar.
Sale is what buses, papers and photographs all do here. Ask her, because the timetable pinned to the wall is from another year.

beats.es: Ese ya se fue, fíjese. El próximo a las dos.
beats.en: The next one, then. That’s fine.
beats.good: El próximo — the next one. There is always a next one, and it leaves when it is full whatever the ticket says.
